name: Davco Ceramaflex
paste:
DAVCO® CERAMAFLEX: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Davco® Ceramaflex, May 2025, Version 01.01 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/5/davco-ceramaflex.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Davco® Ceramaflex where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2025, Version 01.01).
1.2 Product description. Davco® Ceramaflex is a flexible, thin or thick bed, off white, rubber modified cement-based tile adhesive. Davco® Ceramaflex is designed for wall & floor applications for both internal and external applications.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Davco® Ceramaflex is suitable for thin or thickbed applications both internally and externally. SUITABLE TILE TYPES ARE;
    - Ceramic
    - Porcelain
    - Mosaic
    - Terracotta
    - Slate
    - Quarry Tiles
    - Concrete
    - Cement renders
    - Rendered brickwork & blockwork
    - Plasterboard
    - Fibre cement sheet
    - Sika / Davco Approve waterproof membranes
    - Screeds & Mortar beds
    - Early aged screeds (minimum 24 hours @ 22°C & 50% RH)
    - Timber floor (with fibre cement sheet underlay)
    SUITABLE SUBSTRATES INCLUDE;
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.8.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Davco® Ceramaflex
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: A FLEXIBLE, THIN OR THICK BED, OFF WHITE, RUBBER MODIFIED CEMENT-BASED TILE ADHESIVE
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (May 2025, Version 01.01) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - SCAQMD method 304-91: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where: Environmental Information (p.1).
    - AS ISO 13007.1: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Product Declaration (p.1).
    - AS3958.1: referred to in instructions or limitations. Where: Application Instructions > Laying the Tiles (p.3).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Flexible adhesive
    - Economical
    - Good bond strength
    - Off white colour
    - Suitable for early aged screeds
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Appearance / Colour: Off white powder with rubber crumb particles.
    - Product Declaration: C1S1E (AS ISO 13007.1)
2.6 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 20kg Bags / 64 per pallet
    - Shelf life: 12 Months from date of manufacture.
    - Storage conditions: Store in dry cool conditions above ground out of direct sunlight. High humidity will reduce shelf life.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2025, Version 01.01) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality / pre-treatment.
    - Substrate deflection: all substrates under loads shall not exceed L/360 for tiles and L/720 for natural stone.
    - All surfaces must be installed according to manufacturers instructions and relevant standards, and be structurally sound, dry clean and free from movement, oil, grease, wax, sealers, curing compounds or other bond inhibiting material. Thoroughly clean old surfaces or new surfaces that have been treated prior to tiling.
    - Deeply contaminated surfaces require mechanical preparation. Expose at least 80% of the original surface of painted / coated substrates.
    Concrete floors*: Concrete floors shall be a minimum of 6 weeks old. Remove laitance as required. Wood float finished concrete shall be primed with Davco Ultraprime. Steel trowel finished concrete shall be primed with Davco Primex.
    Screeds & Mortar Beds: Screeds & mortar beds shall be a minimum 24 hours old (at 22°C) , sound and not drummy or cracked, with a wood float finish.
    Fibre Cement Sheet / Plaster Board: Sheets shall be fixed in accordance with applicable standards and manufacturers recommendations. Prime sheets with Davco Ultraprime or Primex.
    Compressed Cement boards: Boards shall be soundly fixed in accordance with applicable standards and manufacturers recommendations. Any bond inhibitors shall be removed. Prime boards with Davco Primex. Timber / Particle Board flooring: Timber substrates shall be sheeting with ceramic tile underlay in accordance with manufacturers recommendations. Prime with Davco Ultraprime.
    Existing Tiles: Existing tiles shall be soundly fixed, not drummy or cracked.
    Matt Finished tiles shall be primed with Eco Prep n Prime or Davco Ultrabond (refer to pds for additional information).
    Gloss or shinny tiles shall be primed with Davco Ultrabond, (refer to tds for additional information).
    Other Tile-able Substrates (metal, old flooring, old tile adhesive): Remove all contaminates and bond inhibitors. Prime substrates with Davco Ultrabond (refer to Ultrabond pds for additional information).

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2025, Version 01.01) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing Ratio: 7-8 Litres clean potable water per 20kg bag.
    - Consumption: A 20kg bags cover approximately 14m² with a 6mm notch trowel.
    - Layer Thickness: Maximum layer shall be no greater than 10mm.
    - Pot Life: 1.5 hours
    - Open Time: 30 minutes
    - Adjustability Time: 20 minutes
4.3 Applied Product Ready for Use.
    | Set time before to grouting | 24 hours |
    | Set time before dry area service | 24 hours |
    | Set time before wet area service | 7 days |
    All measurements are taken at 22°C and 50% Relative Humidity. Specifications vary according to site conditions and should be taken as a guide only.
4.4 Equipment. Select a trowel with a suitable notch size for the tile size and type as per the following;
    | Tile Size | Trowel notch size | Back Buttering required |
    | Mosaic's | 4-6mm |
    | 150x150 | 6mm |
    | 200x200 | 8mm | Yes |
    | 300x300 | 10mm | Yes |
    | 400x400 and over | 12mm *as above de- | Yes |
    | *Tiles with lugs or uneven backs Translucent tiles | pendent on size *as above |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
4.5 Mixing.
    - 1. Measure the required amount of clean potable water into a bucket (8 Litres per bag). 2. Slowly add the powder into the water while mixing with a mixing paddle attached to a drill (Max 500 RPM). Do not mix by hand. 3. Continue to mix for 2-3 minutes until a smooth, limp free creamy mixture is achieved. 4. Allow the mixture to stand for 5 minutes then restir for an additional minute.
    - *Adhesive may need restirring during the potlife, do not add more water.
4.6 Application - Laying the Tiles. 1. Place the adhesive onto the prepared and primed substrate. Do not apply more adhesive than can be tiles within the open time of the product, usually from a single tile to 1m². 2. Hold the notched trowel at an angle of 60° or greater to the substrate. 3. Spread the adhesive over the required area where tile is to be applied, comb the adhesive in a single direction (not swirls). 4. Where "back buttering" the tile is required, use the flat side of the notched trowel to apply a thin adhesive layer to the back of the tile (approx 1-2mm thick). 5. Place the tile into the combed adhesive and press the tile firmly. 6. Move the tile forward and then back at 90° across the direction of the combed adhesive to flatten the adhesive to leave no voids under the tile. Occassionally life a tile to check the adhesive covers 90-100% of the tile. 7. Remove any excess adhesive in the joints, and on the face of the tile with a sponge and water while the adhesive is still wet.
    - Do not allow the adhesive to skin prior to placement of the tiles. If the adhesive skins, remove and replace.
    - Application shall be in accordance with AS3958.1
    - Movement joints shall be installed in accordance with applicable standards.
    - Back buttering the tiles may be required to achieve minimum coverage requirements.
    - Allow the adhesive to dry prior to grouting.
4.7 Cleaning of tools. Clean tools and equipment with water orior to adhesive drying.
4.8 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Test product in an inconspicuous area first.
    - When using Davco® Ceramaflex externally or in wet areas ensure correct drainage and falls exist, so that water does not pond on the tile surface.
    - Not suitable for submerged applications.
    - Not suitable for fixing tiles directly onto timber floors
    - For applications above 3 meter high special fixing techniques are required
    - Efflorescence is beyond the control of the manufacturer due to site coniditions beyond our control.
    - For uses not mentioned in this datasheet seek further advice from Sika / Davco Australia.
4.9 Environmental information. Low VOC - 5g/L (SCAQMD method 304-91)

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient Air Temperature. Min +5°C to Max 35°C
5.3 Substrate Temperature. Min +5°C to Max 35°C
5.4 Trials, test areas and compatibility checks stated by the manufacturer.
    - Test product in an inconspicuous area first.
5.5 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Product Declaration: C1S1E (AS ISO 13007.1)
5.6 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.7 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Davco® Ceramaflex, May 2025, Version 01.01, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/5/davco-ceramaflex.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Davco Ceramaflex, version 19/11/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/w/sds-davco-ceramaflex.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage, and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the latest Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological, and other safety related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
